acceptance: A member dispatched as a subagent that attempts `take` on its batch item is refused, shown by a test or a recorded live attempt.
`docs/agent/batch-feature-delivery.md` describes the supported dispatch path; the override used on 2026-11-12 is no longer needed or is documented as policy.
description:
Gap. `docs/agent/batch-feature-delivery.md` says a member never runs as a subagent of its leader, because tractable derives a worker's identity from its MCP server process and subagents share the leader's server, so the tracker cannot tell a member's write from the leader's. The batch `df-distinct-remediation` (PR #4169) ran three members as subagents under an explicit owner override; the members were instructed to make no tracker call and made none, but the `E_BATCH_OWNER` guard and the landing-time tracker-write check gave no protection. The only compliant alternative is the owner starting one top-level session per member, which defeats unattended delivery.

Expected: a supported way for one leader session to dispatch members with distinct tracker identities (for example a per-subagent `TRACTABLE_ACTOR`, or a read-only tracker binding for members), or a documented statement that the override is the accepted practice and what it gives up.

Guardrails: changes to the batch loop are delivered serially and cannot use a batch to certify themselves. Do not weaken `E_BATCH_OWNER` for distinct identities.
